output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses most likely traces to the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not to agency nurses. The new server loaded only 3 of its 14 forwarding rules. The import skipped the other 11 and still reported success. Those rules included a 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 drops, suppression of repeat alerts, and routing of probe-off alarms to the charge phone only. Since 12 August, nurses in Pods A–C get about twice as many phone alerts per shift (80+ versus 38), and acknowledgement times doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, is unchanged. Within Pods A–C, core, agency and new-graduate nurses show similar incident rates. Bedside alarm volume did not change, and there was no step at the 23–24 September monitor update. That argues against the acuity and monitor-software explanations. I'm quite confident (about 90%). Don't approve the agency cap or the performance reviews, because they would punish nurses for a system fault. Re-import the rules with Clinical Engineering validation and Alarm Committee sign-off. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Keep the sick-leave link as a hypothesis for now. Wireless coverage can be checked later if Pods A–C problems persist.
